[[File:Great dodecacronic hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great dodecacronic hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great dodecacronic hexecontahedron''' (or '''great lanceal ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[great dodecicosidodecahedron]]. Its 60 intersecting [[quadrilateral]] faces are [[Kite (geometry)|kites]]. Part of each kite lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

== Proportions ==

Each kite has two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{5}{8}-\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{5})\approx 69.788\,198\,194\,11^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{10}\sqrt{5})\approx 91.512\,394\,720\,74^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{9}{40}\sqrt{5})\approx 128.911\,208\,891\,04^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-19+8\sqrt{5}}{41})\approx 91.553\,403\,672\,16^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long and short edges is <math>\frac{21+3\sqrt{5}}{22}\approx 1.259\,463\,815\,11</math>.
